response.title: Binary search
response.trap_explanation: The student correctly identified that (lo + hi) / 2 can overflow in fixed-width integer languages.

key_points.statement: The input array must be sorted for binary search to work correctly.
key_points.evidence_quote: It would not work correctly on an unsorted array — the halving logic assumes order.

key_points.statement: The lo and hi pointers shrink the search window on every iteration.
key_points.evidence_quote: lo = mid + 1 and hi = mid - 1 move the window closer each time.

key_points.statement: The midpoint value is compared with the target to decide which half to search.
key_points.evidence_quote: I compare arr[mid] to the target, but I wasn't sure about the equal case.

key_points.statement: The loop continues while lo is less than or equal to hi.
The function returns -1 when the target is not found.
key_points.evidence_quote: It returns -1 when the loop ends without finding the target.

key_points.statement: Binary search runs in O(log n) time.
key_points.evidence_quote: I think it's log n because we halve the list each time, but I couldn't prove it.

strengths: Correctly implemented the iterative loop with shrinking bounds.
Identified that an unsorted input breaks the algorithm.
Caught the integer-overflow trap for fixed-width languages.
gaps: Could not articulate the loop-termination condition (lo <= hi) unprompted.
Incomplete explanation of the midpoint comparison for the equal case.
Did not state the O(log n) time complexity without prompting.
review_next: Loop invariants and termination conditions in binary search.
Formal proof of O(log n) complexity.
Edge cases: empty array, single-element array, duplicate values.
